HUMAN AGENCY TRANSFER (SR‑HAT): A Structural Genealogy of How Institutions, Algorithms, and AI Reallocate Effective Human Control

DESCRIPTION

SR‑HAT is a formal SR architecture that explains how effective human control moves across institutional, algorithmic, and AI systems. It defines human agency not as a metaphysical property but as executable control over the stages of decision formation, evidence selection, representation, evaluation, authorization, and execution.

The paper introduces:

  • a historical genealogy of agency allocation

  • a structural saturation mechanism linking load, buffer depletion, and external mediation

  • a stage‑specific control ledger for measuring effective human vs AI control

  • a restoration test that distinguishes capability‑driven delegation from structurally induced transfer

  • a convergence thesis showing how AI unifies previously fragmented agency‑allocation systems

  • falsifiable hypotheses and preregisterable experimental designs

SR‑HAT demonstrates that agency can move without disappearing, and that transfer is not inherently harmful — it becomes structural when human or institutional buffers deteriorate and independent execution becomes costly.

HOW IT CONTRIBUTES TO SR

SR‑HAT is one of the most important transversal components of the SR Ultiverse and SR Systems Psychology. It contributes to the master architecture in five structural ways:

1. It formalizes agency as a measurable SR object

SR‑HAT defines agency as executable control, giving SR a rigorous, testable way to measure:

  • human retained control

  • AI control share

  • platform control

  • institutional control

This becomes essential for Meaning & Agency Science.

2. It provides the mechanism behind Agency‑Substrate Divergence

The Ultiverse predicts divergence between infrastructure, feasible agency, and lived value.
SR‑HAT provides the mechanism:

Load ↑ → Effective capacity ↓ → External mediation ↑ → Agency transfer ↑

This is the structural engine behind Ultiverse Prediction VI.

3. It introduces the Buffer‑Restoration Test

This is one of the strongest causal tests in SR:

Hold AI capability constant. Restore human buffers.
If control returns → structural transfer is real.

This test is crucial for falsification and for SR’s scientific legitimacy.

4. It defines the Agency‑Domain Vector and Convergence Index

These constructs allow SR to:

  • track which agency dimensions become externally allocable

  • measure how AI systems converge multiple agency functions

  • model cross‑metatheory effects in the Ultiverse

This is foundational for transversal SR fields like SR Internet Infrastructure Science.

5. It anchors SR’s predictive claims about behavioural discontinuity and representational substitution

SR‑HAT explains why:

  • behavioural discontinuity can occur before institutional discontinuity

  • representational substitution can alter feasible agency

  • saturation can accelerate machine‑mediated execution

  • restoration requires cross‑metatheory coherence

This directly strengthens Ultiverse Predictions U3, U4, U5, U6, and U7.
